transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-09-29
- Start: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lin (Redwood SE), Jared Morales (Helio Head of ML), Priya Singh (Helio Platform), Mark Davenport (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Integration/discovery focused on integration patterns and compliance needs.

00:00 Olivia Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Olivia with Redwood, this is Marcus our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:18 Jared Morales: Pretty good, thanks. Busy ramping up model features for holiday season so timing's good.
00:28 Olivia Chen: Great. Today we'd like to understand your current stack and integration requirements — especially around SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, and whether you're leaning Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
00:45 Marcus Lin: Quick note, we'll also cover the gateway/proxy option for Private and how observability hooks work.
01:05 Priya Singh: Perfect. From infra side we care about VPC connectivity, KMS integration, and how the proxy sits in front of the models. Latency is important — 95th/99th pcts for interactive features.
01:28 Mark Davenport: Also want to know rate limits and quota controls per team; we have multiple product teams hitting the same endpoints.
01:50 Olivia Chen: Understood. Jared can you give a quick run-through of what you're building and current infra?
02:10 Jared Morales: Sure — we're adding a conversational search assistant across web and in-store tablets. Backend is on AWS; most infra in us-west-2, platform team uses Terraform, infra ppl are in Priya's org. We're prototyping with OpenAI right now but looking for predictable performance and cost — and for Private for PII-sensitive flows.
02:39 Marcus Lin: When you say private for PII can you expand? Are you thinking full on-prem or VPC/private control plane?
02:48 Priya Singh: VPC control plane is preferred; we might consider on-prem later but initial ask is VPC + customer-managed KMS.
03:05 Olivia Chen: Redwood supports Hosted API for quick ramp, Dedicated capacity for predictability, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for data-sensitive workloads. For VPC we offer a gateway/proxy that sits in your VPC and routes requests to the customer-managed control plane — keeps keys in your KMS.
03:35 Jared Morales: Nice, how does the gateway affect latency? It's a concern for our tablet UX.
03:45 Marcus Lin: The gateway is lightweight TCP proxy; in our benchmarks added ~10-20ms typical RTT inside same region, but depends on egress path. For sub-200ms targets we usually recommend Dedicated in-region with the gateway for control. There's also local caching of prefixes to reduce token costs and latency.
04:12 Priya Singh: Cache how — is that something we manage?
04:18 Marcus Lin: It's part of the runtime; prefix / KV cache can be configured per-deployment. If you're using Private with the gateway we can enable local KV cache to avoid round trips for repeated contexts.
04:32 Mark Davenport: What about integrations — we build with Python microservices and a central orchestration that uses LangChain. Any connectors?
04:42 Olivia Chen: Yes we have SDKs for Python and Node, plus official LangChain connectors and example LlamaIndex (now called LlamaIndex in some communities) adapters.
04:55 Marcus Lin: We can share sample notebooks: a LangChain agent using the Redwood Python SDK, and a LlamaIndex ingestion pipeline. Both show batching, streaming, and tool calls.
05:10 Jared Morales: Great, we rely on LlamaIndex for our retrieval layer. Important to preserve embeddings and search latencies. How do embeddings pricing and quotas work?
05:26 Olivia Chen: Embeddings are billed per-unit; quotas can be enforced per API key or per-team by RBAC and rate limits. You can set per-route quotas in the console or via API.
05:38 Priya Singh: For rate limits we need burst capacity for Black Friday traffic spikes. Can we do burst on Dedicated?
05:47 Marcus Lin: Dedicated offers configurable autoscale and burst policies; you can reserve baseline capacity and allow a capped burst. For higher spikes we support fallbacks to hosted instances with controlled throttling and priority routing.
06:06 Mark Davenport: And SSO — we use Okta.
06:10 Olivia Chen: Redwood supports SAML/Okta for console and API access; for audit logs we stream events to customer S3 or SIEM, and Private deployments can write audit logs to your Kinesis/SQS.
06:25 Priya Singh: KMS details? We need to ensure keys never leave our account.
06:30 Marcus Lin: In VPC/private we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM; keys remain in your account and we only receive ciphertext. Full HSM support depending on cloud provider. We'll share the security whitepaper.
07:05 Jared Morales: Cool. On the integration side — what's the dev experience? Are SDKs idiomatic for LangChain?
07:14 Marcus Lin: SDK is similar to OpenAI interface with additional params for routing/pinning. LangChain adapter is a drop-in for most prompt chains; you can pass a 'model_variant' to route requests to Dedicated or Hosted. Example: model_variant: "redwood-dedicated-gptx-2". There are also batching helpers to maximize throughput.
07:45 Jared Morales: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex? We use chunked docs and embeddings at scale.
07:52 Marcus Lin: LlamaIndex integrations are mainly about ingestion to Redwood embeddings API and storing vectors in your vector DB. We provide a LlamaIndex connector that handles chunking, retries, and retries backoff tuned for our rate limits. Occasionally transcription of model names in docs causes mismatch but we've iterated on adapters.
08:20 Priya Singh: Speaking of rate limits, can we throttle per-team keys and see metrics per-route?
08:27 Olivia Chen: Yes — console exposes per-key quotas, per-route SLA tiers, and you can set alerting. Observability gives per-route latency histograms, token-level cost breakdown, and traces for end-to-end requests.
08:46 Mark Davenport: What hooks do you expose for tracing? We use Datadog and OpenTelemetry.
08:52 Marcus Lin: We emit OpenTelemetry spans and have a Datadog integration for ingesting latency traces. There's also a webhook for prompt-level events and a logs forwarder to your logging cluster.
09:05 Jared Morales: Nice. For the POC we want to run a throughput benchmark: 1k concurrent users, 8 requests/sec each during peak with 512-token contexts — can Redwood simulate that?
09:20 Marcus Lin: We can run a benchmark if you provide the prompt set; for Dedicated we can size GPUs for expected RPS and latency. For Private we'll need network topology details. Marcus: noted — we'll need sample prompts and throughput targets (action item).
09:42 Olivia Chen: Pricing — we'll send a baseline pricing for Hosted and Dedicated sizing; Dedicated will include reserved capacity cost and optional burst add-on. Private pricing includes deployment and support.
10:00 Priya Singh: Is there a minimum term for Dedicated?
10:04 Olivia Chen: Typically monthly or annual commitments; annual discounts available. We'll include both options in the spreadsheet.
10:14 Mark Davenport: Security review timeline — our security team will want SOC2 docs and pen-test reports.
10:20 Olivia Chen: We'll share SOC2, ISO docs, and exportable audit log examples. We can set up a security deep-dive with our security PM if needed.
10:35 Jared Morales: What about data retention / delete on demand?
10:40 Marcus Lin: For Private & Dedicated we can configure retention policies and support on-demand deletes for data in the control plane. For Hosted there's configurable retention windows and redaction options.
10:55 Priya Singh: Any network egress considerations for EU customers?
10:58 Olivia Chen: We offer region pinning and data residency controls; for EU-resident data we recommend regional Dedicated or Private.
11:10 Jared Morales: Ok, a few more technicals — SDK support for streaming and function calls?
11:18 Marcus Lin: Yes — streaming responses supported in Python/JS SDKs and function calling as structured outputs. We have examples with LangChain agents that use streaming for token-by-token UI.
11:35 Priya Singh: Can we run some tests against a sandbox before committing?
11:38 Olivia Chen: Absolutely. We'll provision trial keys and a small Dedicated trial node for realistic latency testing.
11:48 Mark Davenport: How long to stand up Dedicated trial?
11:52 Marcus Lin: Typically 48–72 hours once infra details and region are agreed. Private VPC will take longer depending on network config.
12:05 Jared Morales: Sounds good. Any known limitations with the gateway/proxy around websocket streaming?
12:12 Marcus Lin: Websocket streaming works through the gateway; we recommend sticky routing to the same instance for long-lived streams to avoid reconnect overhead. We'll include config samples.
12:30 Olivia Chen: Quick recap on next steps — we'll send pricing + sizing, Marcus will share LangChain/LlamaIndex notebooks, and we'll schedule a Private infra demo with Priya and her infra team. You'll send sample prompt set and peak targets.
12:48 Priya Singh: I'll coordinate and send the prompts.
12:52 Olivia Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week with docs.
12:58 Jared Morales: Thanks, bye.
